paper.title_en: Higher order effects in the SMEFT analysis of $W^+W^−$ production
paper.abstract_en:
This thesis presents a study of the effect of higher dimensional Effective Field Theory (EFT) operators on W +W− production at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC). These operators are studied alongside other higher order Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and Electroweak (EW) corrections to both Standard Model (SM) and Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) predictions. The observable of primary focus in this channel is the dilepton mass distribution Meµ which acts as a proxy for the energy of this process MW W . The latter of which is not observable in this channel due to missing neutrino energy. Furthermore this channel is often analysed in the presence of a jet-veto to reduce tt¯ background.

Chapter 3 presents the contribution of dimension-8 operators to this channel both with a jet-veto at NLL and without a jet-veto at LO. These operators induce a direct gg W +W− contact interaction. The size of these contributions are compared with dimension-6 operators at Λ = 2 TeV. This allows us to better understand the regime of EFT validity for this channel, particularly in the high-energy tails of distributions such as Meµ. We then present constraints and sensitivity studies for dimension-6 and dimension-8 operators with this channel and compare them to those obtained from Higgs studies. We also study the effect of the jet-veto on the quality of future constraints at the LHC for these operators.

Chapter 4 presents work comparing various methods of ensuring EFT validity for constraints in the high energy tails of distributions such as Meµ. We compare three methods: first clipping only the EFT simulation such that MW W < Λ, whilst leaving no cut on the data; second implementing a cut on a transverse mass variable on the data; and finally directly ensuring that dimension-6 contributions are larger than dimension-8 contributions bin by bin. We compare the use of transverse mass distributions with the Meµ distributions for constraints.

Chapter 5 presents a study of bosonic operators which contribute to the qq¯ and γγ induced channels. We study these both with and without a jet-veto to study its effect on constraints. Dimension-6 and dimension-8 operators are compared at NLL accuracy for the first time. We also show that photon induced dimension-8 operators are useful for understanding EFT validity in this channel. We finally present sensitivity studies and constraints for these operator’s Wilson coefficients at a variety scales of new physics (Λ).
